items.title: University Health and Safety Research for the Mining Industry

value.quote: Estimated total funding under this solicitation is $10,000,000, with approximately 5 to 10 awards anticipated.

items.context: Health Research the authority to award competitive contracts and grants to institutions and private entities to improve mine safety and health in general, and specifically to encourage the development and manufacture of mine safety equipment and to award contracts to education institutions or private laboratories for the performance of product testing or related work with respect to new mine technology or equipment. This announcement is an opportunity for the award of contracts to universities in advanced health and safety mining systems. The NIOSH OMSHR is seeking proposals from universities or colleges with ABET-accredited programs in mining engineering specifically focused on aspects of mining safety and health that addresses research, exploratory development, or testing of new innovations and technologies, and/or methods of evaluation of new and existing mining practices to improve mine health and/or safety. The Government has issued similar solicitations previously in mine ventilation (2009-N-11093 and 2014-N15795), ground control (2011-N-13060 and 2016-N-17733), mine design (2019-75D301-19-R-67888), and Mining Systems (2023-75D301-24-R-72911). 41 contracts have been awarded as a result of previous solicitations, resulting in comprehensive contract reports, over 133 M.S. theses and 106 Ph.D. dissertations, and numerous publications (many peer-reviewed), each addressing critical health and safety topics within the mining industry. Under this solicitation, NIOSH continues the expansion of this program to encompass research into broader topics related to advanced mining systems and other critical health and safety research areas including but not limited to mine ventilation and ground control. The Government will award contracts to proposals that provide the greatest value, as determined by the established evaluation criteria. Participants are sought who can train next generation of mine safety and health professionals in development and demonstration of technologies necessary to achieve the objectives outlined in this announcement. 3 Only a Contracting Officer (CO) may obligate the Government to contracts involving expenditure of funds. The Government is not responsible for costs incurred in developing the proposals and is not committed to funding any proposal. Submissions are strictly voluntary. Funding Information The period of performance for all awards shall consist of one base period of 12 months followed by three option periods of 12 months each. Estimated total funding under this solicitation is $10,000,000, with approximately 5 to 10 awards anticipated. Individual awards are limited to a maximum of $300,000 per year and $1,200,000 in total; proposals exceeding these amounts will not be evaluated. Awards will generally be made as firm-fixed-price (FFP) contracts, although the CO may negotiate a fixed price Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 42 U.S.C. 242c when determined to be in the Government's best interest. Grants and cooperative agreements will not be issued under this solicitation. Eligibility Eligible Offerors are U.S. academic institutions with an ABET-accredited undergraduate program in mining engineering based on the ABET Mining Engineering Program Criteria and graduate programs offering both master's and doctoral-level education in mining engineering (or under other names supporting the objectives of this BAA). The proposed Principal Investigator (PI) shall hold a full-time academic appointment at the rank of Assistant/Associate/or Full Professor and shall demonstrate relevant teaching, research, or professional experience in mining safety and health, mining engineering, or another field directly related to the proposed research. There is no limit on the number of proposals that an eligible institution may submit under this BAA. The Government strongly encourages, but does not require, collaboration with mining companies, academic institutions, academic departments, technology developers, research organizations, and other relevant partners. Collaborative efforts may include sharing faculty expertise, students, facilities, datasets, field sites, specialized equipment, or other resources that strengthen the research and graduate educational experience. Participation of faculty, researchers, and graduate students from disciplines outside mining engineering is encouraged when their expertise strengthens the proposed research and expands multidisciplinary capabilities in mine safety and health. Relevant disciplines may include, but are not limited to, computer science, electrical and mechanical engineering, industrial engineering, occupational health and industrial hygiene, public health, materials science, geology, geotechnical engineering, medicine, and other relevant engineering, science, and health fields. Consistent with the capacity-building objectives of this BAA, all graduate students supported under an award shall conduct research directly related to the funded research topic and shall develop their M.S. thesis or Ph.D. dissertation from that research.
